newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 0.9 pct despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 0.9 pct despite profit-taking.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains in selective activity on Thursday, but fell from early highs on profit-taking as the market mostly disregarded the government's second resource package, brokerage.
The IMKB-100 closed up 622.55 points, or 0.92 percent at 68,296.49, but down from a morning high of 68,745. Non-stop gains totalled 5.4 percent so far this week after last week's 2.1 percent rise.
Trade volume jumped to 14.43 trillion lira ($160 million) from Wednesday's 10.83 trillion ($120.2 million).
"The package could not be fully assessed. There was already a need for a pull back after the recent sharp gains," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.
"The market's own dynamics are in charge. It is likely to rise again after easing," he added.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan presented his government's second revenue-raising package aiming to earn another $10 billion. The market mainly awaits implementation of the package.
